investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-10T01:05–01:06Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway — an AWS ELB endpoint at /v1/agents — was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first network call (POST /api/agents → swarm ELB), no evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were ever populated, causing the expected-output contract to be entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" before any agent could be provisioned. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval/observability layer.

investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 744 minutes old, which is 2.48× the contract maximum of 300 minutes. investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot on disk is 744 minutes old at eval time (2026-10-10T01:06:22Z), meaning the last successful publish occurred roughly 12.4 hours prior. The contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) asserts snapshotAgeMinutes max 300; the live evidence value of 744 directly violates this assertion. The check is marked required=false and statusImpact=informational in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 383), so this is an eval-level freshness failure, not a user-facing outage. Add a trend eval that tracks snapshotAgeMinutes over consecutive runs to detect gradual drift (e.g., workflow running less frequently than scheduled) before a hard threshold breach occurs.
